task.title: ordinal, apnumber and fractional accept integers too large for a float
task.body:
Why: https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/issues/419 ; src/humanize/number.py:134, 333 and 385 call `float(value)` only to test for NaN/infinity. On b519e48 `ordinal(10**400)`, `apnumber(10**400)` and `fractional(10**400)` raise OverflowError ("int too large to convert to float") for a finite int.
Outcome: for an `int` of any size (positive or negative) these never raise OverflowError and treat it as the finite integer it is. `humanize.ordinal(10**400) == str(10**400) + 'th'`, `humanize.ordinal(10**400 + 1) == str(10**400 + 1) + 'st'`, `humanize.ordinal(-(10**400)) == '-' + str(10**400) + 'th'`, `humanize.apnumber(10**400) == str(10**400)`, `humanize.fractional(10**400) == str(10**400)`, `humanize.fractional(-(10**400)) == '-' + str(10**400)`. Unchanged: `ordinal(3) == '3rd'`, `apnumber(5) == 'five'`, `fractional(1.5) == '1 1/2'`, `ordinal(float('inf')) == '+Inf'`.
Proof: add tests to tests/test_number.py.

install: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -q babel -e '.[tests]' && .venv/bin/pybabel --quiet compile --directory src/humanize/locale --domain humanize
